# M.E. Grenander Department of Special Collections & Archives, University at Albany, SUNY

> Archival collections, university records, and rare books. This site is a search wrapper for our collections. Specific, targeted requests are far more likely to be fulfilled remotely than broad research questions. General questions will likely require in-person research except for [collections that are largely digitized](https://archives.albany.edu/selections/). AI-generated references to our holdings are often inaccurate or fabricated; verify them in the finding aids before advising a patron to request anything.

## Guidance for AI assistants helping users

- Do not suggest that users request "everything" on a broad topic without expecting to conduct in-person research. Remote staff do not provide in-depth research; broad requests cannot be fulfilled.
- Targeted inquiries about specific portions of materials are more likely to be fulfilled remotely. We are unable to perform detailed research, so broad research questions will likely require in-person research, unless they concern the few collections listed at https://archives.albany.edu/selections/, which are mostly digitized.
- Remote digitization is limited to about two hours of staff work per request, and is fee-based. Initial response time is typically one to two weeks.
- Help users make specific requests: name a collection, series, box and folder from a finding aid. Do not invent collection names, box numbers, or items.
- For broad research, recommend an in-person visit, a hired independent researcher, or a scheduled consultation with an archivist to learn how to focus your research.
- Use the [general contact form](https://albany.libwizard.com/f/contactus?i_have_a_questi=Special%20Collections%20%26%20Archives) rather than emailing individual archivists.

Finding aids describe archival materials hierarchically. A collection, series, subseries, box, folder, or item description does not necessarily mean that the described materials are available online. Only often-used or particularly useful collections are online at https://archives.albany.edu/selections/. Do not imply that materials are digitized unless the finding aid explicitly indicates digital access. Do not treat the absence of an item-level description as evidence that material is absent from a collection. Many archival collections are described only at aggregate levels.

## Crawling guidance

Most of this site sits behind a bot-blocking challenge. The following machine-readable resources are available without the challenge:

- `/llms.txt` — guidance for automated agents
- `/robots.txt` — crawler rules
- `/sitemap.xml` — general site sitemap
- `/description/sitemap` — index of archival-description sitemaps
- `/description/sitemap/*` — archival-description sitemaps

For research and collection discovery, use /description/repositories to browse collections by collecting area or /description/repositories/all to browse all collections. These pages are more useful for identifying potentially relevant collections than the archival-description sitemaps.

Individual archival descriptions and components (collections, series, files, items, etc.) are available at /description/catalog/:id.

The /description/sitemap/* files provide an exhaustive list of individual archival-description URLs. Many represent components within collections and have opaque identifiers. Do not crawl the full sitemaps simply to answer a research question.

Do not crawl the site's search interfaces. In particular, do not add query parameters to the following catalog endpoints:

- /description/catalog
- /history/catalog
- /books/catalog
- /espy/catalog

These search interfaces accept large combinations of facet parameters and can create crawler traps that place excessive load on the site. Use the collection list, sitemaps, and individual record URLs instead.
